cues.en: This video is about learning styles. What kind of learner are you? Oh yeah, I'm a visual person. Oh yeah, same. I think visual learning. Visual. I mean like I remember formulas like auditory. I need to be like interacting with the material. I like to learn by doing myself. Very hands-on. Hands-on learner. Hands-on. So like if I have a model, I'd like to look at that and look it over. Part of this video was sponsored by Google search. There is this idea in education that everyone has their own preferred way of learning. Their so-called learning style.
cues.zh: 这期视频讲学习风格。你是哪种学习者？哦对，我是视觉型的。哦对，我也是。我觉得是视觉学习。视觉。我是说，我记公式像听觉型。我需要和材料互动。我喜欢自己动手学。非常动手实践。动手型学习者。动手。所以比如有个模型，我喜欢看着它、仔细看一遍。本视频部分由 Google Search 赞助。教育界有种观点：每个人都有自己的偏好学习方式，也就是所谓的学习风格。

cues.en: If information is presented in accordance with the learning style, then they'll learn better. Now, there are dozens of different learning style theories, but the most common one identifies four main learning styles. Visual, auditory, reading-writing, and kinesthetic, or VARC for short. Visual learners learn best from images, demonstrations, and pictures. People may say things, but I can't really like take it in. I just got to see them act it out or write it.
cues.zh: 如果信息按学习风格来呈现，他们就会学得更好。现在有几十种不同的学习风格理论，但最常见的一种划分出四种主要学习风格：视觉型、听觉型、读写型和动觉型，简称 VARC。视觉型学习者通过图像、演示和图片学得最好。别人说东西，我可能真吸收不进去。我就得看他们演出来或写出来。

cues.en: Auditory learners learn best from listening to an explanation. Like in school, I was always engaged in a lecture and that was usually good enough to pass a test. Reading writing learners learn best from reading and writing. Like I can get pretty much anything out of reading a textbook or something. And kinesthetic learners learn best by doing, physically interacting with the world. Hands-on, you have to touch things, you have to play with things. You know, it's a contact sport. You have to do it yourself. I want to try something with you.
cues.zh: 听觉型学习者通过听讲解学得最好。比如在学校，我上课总能听进去，通常光这样就能通过考试。读写型学习者通过阅读和写作学得最好。比如读教科书之类的，我几乎什么都能学到。动觉型学习者通过动手、与物理世界互动学得最好。动手，你得摸东西，得摆弄东西。你知道，这是项接触性运动。你得亲自做。我想和你试个东西。

cues.en: A little experiment. I want to show you 10 pictures of things, and I don't want you to say anything while you're looking at them. And at the end of the 10, you tell me how many you can remember. Okay. Okay? Okay. Okay. Now, learning styles make intuitive sense because we know everyone is different. Some people have better spatial reasoning, others have better listening comprehension.
cues.zh: 做个小实验。我想给你看 10 张物品图片，你看的时候什么都别说。看完这 10 张，你告诉我能记住几个。好。可以吗？好。好。学习风格直觉上说得通，因为我们知道每个人都不同。有些人空间推理更好，有些人听力理解更好。

cues.en: We know some people are better readers, while others are good with their hands. It sort of very much fits with a broad strain of thought in sort of what the recent Western tradition is, like we're all unique, we're all different. And so you don't want to say, like, everybody learns the same way. That sort of conflicts with our feelings about what it means to be human. So doesn't it make sense that people should learn better in their own preferred learning style? Well, teachers certainly seem to think so.
cues.zh: 我们知道有些人更擅长阅读，有些人手很巧。这很符合一种广泛的思想脉络，算是近代西方传统的一部分：我们都是独特的，我们都各不相同。所以你不会想说，每个人学习方式都一样。那会和我们关于何为人类的感觉相冲突。那么，人们按自己偏好的学习风格来学，难道不是应该学得更好吗？嗯，老师们显然好像这么认为。

cues.en: A survey of nearly 400 teachers from the UK and the Netherlands found that over 90% believed that individuals learn better when they receive information in their preferred learning style. Just like every professor has a different style of teaching, you have a different style of learning. But when his teacher starts using visuals, Jonathan finds it easier to focus and understand the material, so he might be a visual learner. Can you tell me what that means to you? What does it mean to be a visual learner?
cues.zh: 一项针对英国和荷兰近 400 名教师的调查发现，超过 90% 的人认为，当个体以偏好的学习风格接收信息时会学得更好。就像每位教授都有不同的教学风格，你也有不同的学习风格。但当老师开始使用视觉材料时，Jonathan 发现自己更容易集中注意力并理解内容，所以他可能是视觉型学习者。你能告诉我这对你意味着什么吗？成为视觉型学习者意味着什么？

cues.en: To me, it means that for me to learn something, sometimes I need to draw it, or I need to write it down, or I need to see a picture or a movie. For example, science classes, I get bored easily just listening, and I think it's more interesting for me to actually be able to do it. How do you know that you're a visual learner? I don't. I just assume. To take advantage of learning styles, then teachers need to do two things. First, identify the learning style of each of their students. And second,
cues.zh: 对我来说，这意味着要想学会某样东西，我有时得把它画下来，或者写下来，或者看图片、看视频。比如科学课，光听我很容易犯困，如果能亲自上手操作，我觉得会更有意思。你怎么知道自己是视觉型学习者呢？我不知道，只是这么推测。要利用好学习风格，老师需要做两件事：第一，识别每个学生的学习风格；第二，

cues.en: teach each student in accordance with their learning style. On the VARC website it says, once you know about VARC, its power to explain things will be a revelation. But before you take an online learning styles quiz, it's a good idea to ask, do learning styles even exist? I mean, do you have one? And if you're taught in accordance with it, would you learn better?
cues.zh: 针对每个学生的学习风格因材施教。VARC 官网上写着：一旦你了解了 VARC，它解释事物的能力会让你豁然开朗。但是在你做网上的学习风格测试之前，最好先问一句：学习风格真的存在吗？我是说，你有属于自己的学习风格吗？如果按照这种风格来教你，你真的能学得更好吗？

cues.en: Well, you could test this by running a randomized control trial, where first you would identify learners with at least two different learning styles, say visual and auditory, and then randomly assign the learners to one of two educational presentations, one visual, one auditory. So for half of the students, the experience will match their learning style, and for the other half, it won't. And then you give everyone the same test.
cues.zh: 你可以通过随机对照试验来验证这一点：首先找出至少有两种不同学习风格的学习者，比如视觉型和听觉型，然后把他们随机分配到两种教学展示方式中的一种，一种是视觉的，一种是听觉的。这样一来，有一半学生的教学体验符合他们的学习风格，而另一半则不符合。最后让所有人做同一套测试。

cues.en: If the learning style hypothesis is correct, the results should show better performance when the presentation matches the learning style than when they're mismatched. I tried a very unscientific version of this experiment on the street. For some people, I matched their learning style, so I showed visual learners pictures of 10 items. But for other visual learners, I read out the items instead.
cues.zh: 如果学习风格假说是正确的，那么教学方式与学习风格匹配时的表现，应该明显好于不匹配时。我在街头做了一个非常不严谨的实验版本。对一部分人，我匹配了他们的学习风格，给视觉型学习者展示了 10 种物品的图片；但对另一部分视觉型学习者，我则是把这些物品念给他们听。

cues.en: Sun. Okay, I'm maxed out. How many can you remember? Pair, knife, duck, heart, butterfly. Apple, bicycle, guitar. There's a spider. Did I say I already? Trumpet. Pair, butterfly, duck, boat, heart.
cues.zh: 太阳。好了，到极限了。你能记住几个？梨、小刀、鸭子、爱心、蝴蝶。苹果、自行车、吉他。还有只蜘蛛。我是不是说过了？小号。梨、蝴蝶、鸭子、小船、爱心。

cues.en: Couldn't tell you the rest. That's all I got. Most people could remember only about five or six things. Six. Six is not bad. Six out of ten. Which is not bad. That's a passing score. But a few could remember substantially more. Say eight or nine items. Bug. I don't know if I said bug. I feel like I fell, spoon, sun, chair.
cues.zh: 剩下的想不起来了。我就记得这些。大多数人只能记住五六样东西。六个。六个还不错。十个里中了六个。还挺不错的，算及格了。但少数人能记住多得多，比如八九样。虫子。不知道我说没说过虫子。感觉我……勺子、太阳、椅子。

cues.en: I'm forgetting the last two. That's pretty good. Eight is really good. Oh cool. Nine? Nine. Very impressive. But the reason didn't seem to be because the presentation matched their preferred learning style but because they employed a memory strategy. So like as you were showing I was like making an order in my head so as I saw more I would just add it to the list and I was repeating the list as I was looking at them so I could just say it out loud. Did you try a strategy while you were...
cues.zh: 最后两个忘了。已经相当不错了。八个真的很厉害。太棒了。九个吗？九个。太厉害了。但原因似乎并不是教学方式匹配了他们偏好的学习风格，而是他们使用了记忆策略。“就是你展示的时候，我在脑子里排了个顺序，看到新的就加进去，一边看一边默念，这样我就能直接背出来。”你在……的时候也用了策略吗？

cues.en: This is obviously anecdotal evidence, but rigorous studies like the one I outlined have been conducted. For example, one looked at visualizers versus verbalizers instead of visual versus auditory learners. The study was computer-based.
cues.zh: 这显然只是个例，但也确实有人做过像我刚才提到的那种严谨研究。比如有一项研究考察的是“视觉型”与“语言型”学习者，而非视觉型与听觉型。该研究是基于电脑进行的。

cues.en: So first, students' learning styles were assessed using questions like, would you rather read a paragraph or see a diagram describing an atom? The researchers also provided some challenging explanations with two buttons, visual help or verbal help. The visual one played a short animation, whereas the verbal help gave a written explanation.
cues.zh: 首先，研究人员通过类似“你更想读一段文字，还是看一张原子示意图？”这样的问题来评估学生的学习风格。他们还提供了一些有难度的解释内容，并配有两个按钮：“视觉帮助”和“语言帮助”。点击视觉帮助会播放一段简短动画，而语言帮助则提供书面解释。

cues.en: From these measures combined, the researchers categorized the students as either visualizers or verbalizers. And then the students were randomly assigned to go through a text-based or picture-based lesson on electronics. When a student hovered their mouse over keywords in the lesson in the text-based group, a definition and clarification came up. But in the picture group, an annotated diagram was shown instead. And after the lesson, the students did a test to assess their learning.
cues.zh: 结合这些测试，研究人员将学生归类为视觉型或语言型。随后，学生被随机分配去学习一门以文本为主或以图片为主的电子学课程。在文本组中，学生将鼠标悬停在课程关键词上时，会弹出定义和说明；而在图片组中，显示的则是一张带标注的示意图。学完之后，学生接受了测试以评估学习效果。

cues.en: The students whose preferred learning style matched their instruction performed no better on the tests than those whose instruction was mismatched. The researchers ran the test again with 61 non-college educated adults and found exactly the same result. But learning styles are a preference. So how strongly do learners stick to their preference?
cues.zh: 偏好学习风格与教学方式相匹配的学生，在测试中的表现并不比不匹配的学生更好。研究人员又对 61 名没有大学学历的成年人重复了这项测试，得到了完全相同的结果。但学习风格只是一种偏好，那么学习者坚持自己偏好的程度到底有多高呢？

cues.en: Well, in a 2018 study during the first week of semester, over 400 students at a university in Indiana completed the VARC questionnaire, and they were classified according to their learning style. Then at the end of the semester, the same students completed a study strategy questionnaire. So, how did they actually study during the term?
cues.zh: 在 2018 年的一项研究中，开学第一周，印第安纳州一所大学的 400 多名学生填写了 VARC 问卷，并按学习风格进行了分类。到了学期末，这批学生又填写了一份学习策略问卷。那么，他们在这学期里实际上是怎么学习的呢？

cues.en: Well, an overwhelming majority of students used study strategies which were supposedly incompatible with their learning style, and the minority of students who did, did not perform significantly differently on the assessments in the course. The Visual Auditory Reading Writing Kinesthetic, or VARC model, came about from Neil Fleming, a school inspector in New Zealand. Describing the origins of VARC, he says,
cues.zh: 结果绝大多数学生采用的学习策略，按理说都与他们的学习风格不符；而少数相符的学生，在课程考核中的表现也没有显著差异。视觉、听觉、读写、动觉，即 VARC 模型，源自新西兰的一位学校督学 Neil Fleming。在描述 VARC 的起源时，他说道：

cues.en: I was puzzled when I observed excellent teachers who did not reach some learners, and poor teachers who did. I decided to try to solve this puzzle. There are, of course, many reasons for what I observed, but one topic that seemed to hold some magic, some explanatory power, was preferred modes of learning, modal preferences. And thus, Vark was born.
cues.zh: “当我看到优秀的老师教不好某些学生，而水平较差的老师反而能教会时，我感到很困惑。我决定试着解开这个谜团。我观察到的现象当然有很多原因，但似乎有一个很有魔力、很有解释力的话题，那就是‘偏好的学习模式’，即模态偏好。就这样，Vark 诞生了。”

cues.en: There was no study that revealed students naturally cluster into four distinct groups, just some magic that might explain why some teachers can reach students while others can't. But how can this be? If we accept that some people are more skilled at interpreting and remembering certain kinds of stimuli than others, like visual or auditory, then why don't we see differences in learning or recall with different presentations?
cues.zh: 没有任何研究表明学生会自然地分成四个截然不同的群体，那只是一种看似合理的说法，试图解释为什么有些老师教得好，有些却教不好。但这怎么可能呢？如果我们承认某些人比其他人更擅长理解和记忆某种刺激（比如视觉或听觉刺激），那为什么换用不同的呈现方式时，我们却看不到学习效果或记忆表现上的差异？

cues.en: Well, it's because what we actually want people to recall is not the precise nature of the images or the pitch or quality of the sound, it's the meaning behind the presentations. There are some tasks that obviously require the use of a particular modality. Learning about music, for example, should have an auditory component. Similarly, learning about geography will involve looking at maps. And some people will have greater aptitude to learn one task over another. Someone with perfect pitch, for example, will be better able to recall certain tones in music.
cues.zh: 这是因为我们真正希望人们记住的，并不是图像的具体特征，或是声音的音高与音质，而是呈现内容背后的含义。有些任务显然需要特定的感官形式。比如学音乐肯定包含听觉成分，同样，学地理也离不开看地图。而且有些人确实在某些任务上比别人更有天赋。例如，拥有绝对音高的人能更好地记住音乐中的特定音调。

cues.en: Someone with excellent visuospatial reasoning will be better at learning the locations of countries on a map. But the claim of learning style theories is that these preferences will be consistent across learning domains. The person with perfect pitch should learn everything better auditorily. But that is clearly not the case. Most people will learn geography better with a map. Review articles of learning styles consistently conclude there is no credible evidence that learning styles exist.
cues.zh: 视觉空间推理能力强的人，能更快掌握地图上各国的位置。但“学习风格”理论主张的是：这些偏好在所有学习领域中都是一致的。照此说法，有绝对音高的人不管学什么用听的都该学得更好。但这显然不是事实。大多数人学地理时看地图效果都更好。关于学习风格的综述文献一致认为：没有任何可靠证据表明学习风格的存在。

cues.en: In a 2009 review, the researchers note the contrast between the enormous popularity of the learning styles approach within education and the lack of credible evidence for its utility is, in our opinion, striking and disturbing. If classification of students' learning styles has practical utility, it remains to be demonstrated. What we're expecting is if your style was honored, you're going to perform better than if you had some experience that conflicted with your style. And this is where
cues.zh: 在 2009 年的一篇综述中，研究人员指出：“在教育界，学习风格方法的风靡程度与缺乏可靠效用证据之间的反差，在我们看来令人震惊且深感不安。对学生学习风格的划分是否具有实用价值，仍有待证明。”我们本以为，如果迎合了你的风格，你的表现就会优于那些违背你风格的学习方式。而这正是……

cues.en: We don't see any support for the learning styles theory. One of the reasons many people find learning styles so convincing is because they already believe it to be true.
cues.zh: 我们找不到任何支持学习风格理论的证据的地方。很多人觉得学习风格非常有说服力，原因之一是他们早就先入为主地相信了。

cues.en: For example, they might already think that they're a visual learner. And then when a teacher shows them a diagram of, say, a bike pump and suddenly the concept clicks, well, they interpret this as evidence for their visual learning style. You already believe that learning styles is right. When you have an experience, the first thing you think is, is that in some way consistent with learning styles? And if it is, you don't think further. When in reality, that diagram might just be a great diagram that would have helped anyone learn.
cues.zh: 例如，他们可能自认为是个“视觉型学习者”。当老师拿出一张比如自行车打气筒的图解，让他们突然豁然开朗时，他们就会把这当成自己是视觉型学习者的证据。你既然认定学习风格是对的，有了这种经历，你脑海里冒出的第一个念头就是：这不正好符合学习风格理论吗？一旦对上号，你就不再深思了。可事实上，那张图可能本身就非常出色，换成谁来看都能学得更快。

cues.en: When we already believe the world to be a certain way, then we interpret new experiences to fit with those beliefs whether they actually do or not. So if learning styles don't improve learning, then what does? Well, there's a large body of literature that supports the claim that everyone learns better with multimodal approaches, where words and pictures are presented together rather than either words or pictures alone. Now there's going to be words as well as the picture. We're going to see if this is any better.
cues.zh: 当我们已经相信世界是某种样子时，就会把新体验解释成符合这些信念的样子，不管它们实际上是否符合。那么，如果学习风格不能提升学习效果，什么能呢？有大量文献支持这一说法：每个人都能通过多模态方法学得更好，也就是文字和图片一起呈现，而不是只给文字或只给图片。现在既有文字也有图片。我们来看看这样是否更好。

cues.en: This is known as the multimedia effect, and it explains, in part, at least why videos can be such powerful tools for learning, when the narration complements the visuals. In my PhD research, I found explicit discussion of misconceptions was essential in multimedia teaching for introductory physics.
cues.zh: 这被称为多媒体效应，它至少部分解释了为什么当旁白与画面互补时，视频能成为如此强大的学习工具。在我的博士研究中，我发现对于入门物理的多媒体教学，明确讨论错误概念至关重要。

cues.en: Ultimately, the most important thing for learning is not the way the information is presented, but what is happening inside the learner's head. People learn best when they're actively thinking about the material, solving problems or imagining what happens if different variables change. I talked about how and why we learn best in my video, The Science of Thinking, so check that out.
cues.zh: 归根结底，学习最重要的不是信息呈现方式，而是学习者头脑中正在发生什么。当人们积极思考材料、解决问题，或想象不同变量变化会发生什么时，学习效果最好。我在视频《思考的科学》中谈过我们如何以及为何学得最好，可以去看看。

cues.en: Now, the truth is, there are many evidence-based teaching methods that improve learning. Learning styles is just not one of them. And it is likely, given the prevalence of the learning style's misconception, that it actually makes learning worse. I mean, learning styles give teachers unnecessary things to worry about, and they may make some students reluctant to engage with certain types of instruction.
cues.zh: 事实上，有很多基于证据的教学方法能提升学习效果。学习风格并不在其中。考虑到学习风格迷思如此普遍，它很可能实际上让学习变得更糟。我的意思是，学习风格让老师操心不必要的事情，还可能让一些学生不愿参与某些类型的教学。

cues.en: And all the time and money spent on learning styles and related training could be better spent on interventions that actually improve learning. You are not a visual learner, nor an auditory learner, nor a kinesthetic learner. Or, more accurately, you are all these kinds of learner in one. The best learning experiences are those that involve multiple different ways of understanding the same thing. And best of all, this strategy works not just for one subset of people, but
cues.zh: 花在学习风格及相关培训上的所有时间和金钱，本可以更好地用于真正能提升学习的干预措施。你不是视觉型学习者，也不是听觉型或动觉型学习者。更准确地说，你同时是所有这些类型的学习者。最好的学习体验，是用多种不同方式理解同一件事。最棒的是，这种策略不只对某一小部分人有效，而是

cues.en: for everyone. This part of the video was sponsored by Google Search. Now there are lots of topics out there that are controversial, like learning styles, for example. Most people believe learning styles are a thing, whereas educational researchers find no robust evidence for them. And if you search for learning styles, you'll get lots of sites with resources and quizzes. But if you search for learning styles debunked, well then you'll find articles about how there is very little evidence for the learning styles hypothesis. I think...
cues.zh: 对所有人都有效。本视频这一部分由 Google Search 赞助。现在有很多有争议的话题，比如学习风格。大多数人相信学习风格确有其事，而教育研究者却没有发现支持它的有力证据。如果你搜索“learning styles”，会得到很多提供资源和测验的网站。但如果你搜索“learning styles debunked”，就会找到一些文章，说明学习风格假说几乎没有证据支持。我觉得……

cues.en: One of the most common traps people fall into is only searching for information that confirms what they already believe. A common mistake is putting the answer you're looking for right in the search query. A better idea is to try another search, adding debunked or false at the end, and see what comes up. And Google makes it easy to get more detail about the source of the information. Just click the three dots next to any search result, and then you can judge for yourself whether the information is trustworthy and if you want to visit the site.
cues.zh: 最容易踩的一个坑，就是只去搜索能印证自己既有观点的信息。一个常见的错误是直接把想要的答案写进了搜索框里。更好的做法是换个方式再搜搜，比如在末尾加上 debunked（辟谣）或 false（造假），看看会出来什么。而且 Google 能让你很轻松地了解信息来源的详细背景。只需点击搜索结果旁边的三个点，你就能自行判断这些信息是否可信，以及是否要访问该网站。

cues.en: A Google search is meant to surface the most relevant information for your query. But it's up to you to formulate that query, try a few different searches, and assess whether the information is reliable. And the whole point of Veritasium is to get to the truth. So I'm excited to encourage everyone to think more critically about how we get information. I want to thank Google for sponsoring this part of the video, and I want to thank you for watching.
cues.zh: Google 搜索的初衷是为你呈现与查询最相关的信息。但如何组织查询语句、尝试多种不同的搜索方式，以及评估信息是否可靠，关键还在于你自己。而 Veritasium 的核心宗旨就是探寻真相。所以我也很乐于借此鼓励大家，在获取信息时多一些批判性思考。感谢 Google 对本期视频这部分内容的赞助，也感谢大家的观看。
